title: Tencent Hy4 Flash Lands on Fireworks: Professional Tasks Done as Well as Claude, at 200 Times Lower Cost

content_html:
Tencent's open-source model Hy4Flash has found a new foothold on an international cloud inference platform. This mixture-of-experts model is now officially available on the Fireworks serverless platform—it has about 220 billion total parameters, activates only about 12 billion per token, supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens (512K at launch), and can ingest both text and images. Its positioning is quite clear: it was built for professional scenarios such as document processing, research, office work, and agentic workflows, selling "good-enough intelligence" at the lowest possible price.

Fireworks put it through a real, no-nonsense checkup. On every Specialized Intelligence Index benchmark that tracks cost, Hy4Flash sits on the score-cost Pareto frontier—put plainly, on these leaderboards, no model can deliver a higher score for less money. The most telling example is Epiq's CorporateBench: this test evaluates a model's ability to answer questions across thousands of internal company emails and meeting notes. Hy4Flash scored 75.9%, ranking 6th out of 14 models and narrowly beating Claude Opus5.5's 75.4%; the billing gap is staggering—it costs only $0.013 per task, while Opus5.5 costs $2.80, more than 200 times cheaper, making it the lowest-cost contender on the entire leaderboard.

Its other two report cards are just as impressive. On Rogo's large finance benchmark, Hy4Flash tied Claude Opus5 at 49.2%, but the former costs $0.0065 per task while the latter costs $1.83—a gap of about 280 times—and it also edged past Claude Opus5.5 and Kimi K3.1Pro (both 48.2%). The only model on the leaderboard cheaper than it, GPT-6Luna, scored just 35.3%. On Sierra's banking-oriented agent benchmark τ³-Banking, it essentially tied Claude Opus5, edging it 49.2% to 49.1%, at a cost of $0.012 per trial versus $2.59. On general capabilities, it scored 96.67 on AIME2026, 91.92 on GPQA Diamond, and 90.60 on SWE-bench Verified—all top-tier levels within the open-source camp.

Of course, this ledger also has some unflattering pages. Hy4Flash ranks lower on HealthBench Professional (16th out of 18 models) and DeepSWE (19th out of 22 models), and for long-horizon software engineering tasks, Tencent itself recommends simply switching to the larger Hy4. On pricing, Fireworks charges $0.07 per million input tokens, $0.003 for cache hits, and $0.281 for output; it also offers a higher-priority Priority tier, is available globally, and supports everything from lightweight fine-tuning to full-parameter training. When the unit price of "specialized intelligence" is driven to the industry's lowest, the question in this race is quietly being rewritten—it is no longer just about who is smarter, but also about whose intelligence is more cost-effective.
